sourcesNote: Names, descriptions and grades are the official PlayStation 5 list as Exophase and PSNProfiles listed it; the two agree on every name, description and grade. Counts (such as 42 Shooting Range challenges) are PSN's counts as PSNProfiles lists them. Every guide below is written in our own words from the official description; where a place or step is not pinned down by a source we have checked, the guide says so.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide:
The platinum. It unlocks automatically the moment the other 54 trophies are earned — there is nothing extra to do for it, and no separate task hides behind it.

Treat it as the finish line, not a trophy to chase directly: work the roadmap in order (story, strangers, collectibles, activities, then the 100% clean-up) and this one pops when the last of the 54 lands. If one trophy is left, the checklist's filters will show it — filter by the kind you have been putting off.
steps: Earn the other 54 trophies.
The platinum unlocks automatically when the last one pops.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade). Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide:
The opening mission. Play through Gone Fishing from the start of the story and finish it — the trophy pops when the mission completes, and it is the first story trophy most players will earn.

No preparation is needed and nothing here can be missed: it is a story mission, and story missions can be replayed if anything goes wrong. If you are just starting out, this is your first tick on the checklist.
steps: Start the story and play the opening mission, Gone Fishing.
Finish the mission to its end screen.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade). Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide:
Finish every mission in Chapter 1. The trophy is tied to the chapter, not to any single mission, so it pops when the last mission of the chapter ends — you cannot earn it early by skipping ahead.

Play the chapter in order and watch for the chapter-complete beat. Nothing in a chapter trophy can be missed: chapters are story progress, and story missions can be replayed.
steps: Play through Chapter 1's missions in order.
Finish the chapter's final mission.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade). Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide:
Finish every mission in Chapter 2. Like the other chapter trophies, this one pops when the chapter's final mission ends — it is a progress marker, not a challenge with its own conditions.

Keep playing the story in order after Chapter 1. The name is printed exactly as PlayStation publishes it, asterisks included. Nothing here can be missed.
steps: Play through Chapter 2's missions in order.
Finish the chapter's final mission.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade). Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide:
Finish every mission in Chapter 3. The trophy pops at the end of the chapter's final mission, as the story moves on to Chapter 4.

By this point the game's systems — driving, combat, the wanted system — are all in play, so if any activity trophy needs a mechanic you have not tried yet, Chapter 3 is a good place to practise it. Nothing in this trophy can be missed.
steps: Play through Chapter 3's missions in order.
Finish the chapter's final mission.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade). Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide:
Finish every mission in Chapter 4, the last chapter. This is the final chapter trophy before the story's closing mission, so earning it means you are one mission away from the gold for the finale.

Do the missable one-off moments flagged in this guide before you finish the story, while the missions that carry them are still in front of you. Nothing in this chapter trophy itself can be missed.
steps: Play through Chapter 4's missions in order.
Finish the chapter's final mission.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade). Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide:
Finish the story's final mission. This is one of only two gold trophies in the game, and it marks the end of the main story — after it, the whole map stays open for the collectibles, activities and clean-up stages of the roadmap.

Before you start the finale, check the Missables view: the one-off moments in this guide belong to the story, and the finale is the last chance for any that only happen during missions. The trophy itself cannot be missed — the final mission can be replayed.
steps: Complete Chapters 1 to 4.
Play and finish the final mission.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade). Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide:
Finish the story mission Breakfast Run. Mission trophies pop when the mission's end screen appears, whatever rating you get — you do not need a perfect run or a medal.

If a mission ever fails, retry it from the mission menu; story missions can be replayed, so a failed attempt costs nothing but time. No location beyond the mission itself is involved, and the official description pins nothing else down.
steps: Reach the mission Breakfast Run in the story.
Complete it to its end screen.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade). Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide:
Finish the story mission The Cartel Heist. Heist missions in GTA games are usually longer, multi-part jobs — expect setup beats before the heist itself, and play them in the order the game presents them.

The trophy needs only the completion, not a particular approach or rating. If the heist fails part-way, retry from the checkpoint or the mission menu. Nothing here can be missed.
steps: Reach the mission The Cartel Heist in the story.
Complete it to its end screen.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade). Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide:
Finish the story mission Child's Play. The trophy pops at the mission's end screen, with no extra condition attached to the description.

Play the story in order and it will come to you — there is no side requirement to unlock it. If you fail the mission, retry it; story missions can be replayed.
steps: Reach the mission Child's Play in the story.
Complete it to its end screen.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade). Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide:
Finish the story mission Headliners. The name hints at a high-profile job, but the official description asks for nothing more than completing the mission — no rating, no optional objective.

Just play it through. A failed attempt can be retried from the mission menu, and the trophy cannot be missed.
steps: Reach the mission Headliners in the story.
Complete it to its end screen.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade). Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide:
Finish the story mission VCIA Takedown, set around Vice City International Airport. The trophy needs only the mission's completion.

Do not confuse this with the separate VCIA moment trophy (Catch Me If You Can) — that one is about leaving the airport in an unscheduled way, and it is flagged missable in this guide. This mission trophy itself cannot be missed.
steps: Reach the mission VCIA Takedown in the story.
Complete it to its end screen.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade). Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide:
Finish the story mission Operation Savage Glory. The operation name suggests a large set-piece, but the trophy's only condition is finishing the mission.

Play it in story order, retry from a checkpoint if it fails, and the trophy pops at the end screen. Nothing here can be missed.
steps: Reach the mission Operation Savage Glory in the story.
Complete it to its end screen.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade). Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide:
Reach 100% completion on the game's in-game checklist. This is the second gold trophy and, for most players, the last one before the platinum — it is the trophy that forces the clean-up.

100% in GTA games is a fixed checklist the game itself tracks (story, stranger missions, collectibles, activities and the counted feats). Work the roadmap in order and keep an eye on the game's own completion percentage; when it reads 100%, this pops. Do not guess at what counts — the in-game checklist is the source of truth, and this guide's stages map onto it.
steps: Finish the story and the stranger strands.
Complete the collectibles, activities and counted feats the game's 100% checklist tracks.
Check the in-game completion percentage until it reads 100%.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade). Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide:
Pull off 250 stunts. A stunt is a driving feat the game recognises — jumps, near misses, long airtime, that kind of moment — and the count is cumulative across the whole playthrough, so every stunt you have already done counts toward the 250.

Do not grind this from zero: play the story first and let the count build naturally, then finish the remainder by chaining jumps and airtime on open roads. The official description gives the target (250) but no list of which moves count, so use the game's own stunt feedback on screen as the check for what registers.
steps: Play the story; stunts accumulate as you drive.
Chain jumps and airtime on open roads to finish the remaining count.
Check the PSN progress counter toward 250.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade); PSN count 250 — PSNProfiles. Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide:
Try every type of activity in the game once. The starter list counts 9 activity types, and the trophy pops when you have sampled the last one — you do not need to win, finish or master any of them, just try each.

Work through the activity icons on the map one by one: racing, the shooting range, fishing, drone racing, arcade games, bowling and the rest, until the last type is tried. The official description does not name the 9 types, so the in-game activity list is the checklist to work from — do not trust a list from memory.
steps: Open the map and note each activity type.
Try each type once.
The trophy pops when the last untried type is sampled.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade); 9 types as the kit's starter list counts them. Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide:
Earn a gold medal in all 42 Shooting Range challenges. There are 42 challenges in total, and every one of them needs gold — a silver or bronze in even one leaves this trophy locked.

This is the hardest pure-skill trophy in the set, so save it for after the story when your aim and weapon handling are practised. Work through the range's challenges one weapon at a time, replay any challenge that falls short of gold, and use the range's own medal display to see which ones are still missing gold. No location beyond the Shooting Range itself is involved, and the official description pins nothing else down.
steps: Find the Shooting Range and open its challenge list.
Earn gold in each of the 42 challenges, replaying any that fall short.
Check the range's medal display until all 42 show gold.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade); PSN count 42 challenges — PSNProfiles. Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide:
Win a Top Fun drone race at all 14 locations. Each location has its own race, and you need a win at every one — winning the same location twice does not help.

Fly each course once to learn its gates and turns, then race it for the win; a loss can simply be retried. The official description gives the count (14 locations) but does not name them, so use the Top Fun markers on the in-game map as the list — tick each location off as you win it.
steps: Find each Top Fun drone race location on the map.
Win the race at each of the 14 locations.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade); PSN count 14 locations — PSNProfiles. Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide:
Win 20 different races. The word different matters: the same race won twice counts once, so you need wins on 20 distinct race events across the map.

Work through the race markers one by one and keep a note of which you have won — this checklist's export can hold your notes if you use the search to find this trophy. Races can be retried freely after a loss, and nothing here can be missed.
steps: Find race events on the map.
Win 20 distinct races, one win per event.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade); PSN count 20 — PSNProfiles. Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide:
Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Cal is the named rival for this one — find the fishing challenge where he is the opponent and out-fish him.

Fishing challenges can be retried, so a loss is just a retry, not a miss. The official description names the opponent (Cal) but no fishing spot, so use the fishing challenge markers in the game to find where Cal waits — do not guess at a spot the description does not name.
steps: Find a fishing challenge against Cal.
Beat him in the challenge; retry on a loss.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade). Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide:
Complete one arcade game — any game, at any arcade. Finishing a game is enough; you do not need a high score or a win against anyone.

Pick the shortest arcade game you can find and play it to its end. This is one of the quickest activity trophies, and a good first tick in the activities stage.
steps: Find an arcade.
Play any arcade game through to its end.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade). Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide:
Complete Andy's final mission. Andy is one of the named characters with a mission strand of their own — play their missions in order until the strand ends.

Character finales unlock as you progress their strands; if Andy's missions are not showing yet, keep playing the story and check the map for the character's marker. The trophy pops at the final mission's end screen, and it cannot be missed.
steps: Follow Andy's mission strand on the map.
Complete Andy's final mission.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade). Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide:
Complete Kenton's final mission. Like the other character finales, this is the end of a strand of missions for a named character — play them in the order the game offers them.

The name hints at a boat, but the official description asks only for the final mission's completion, so do not read a location or a method into it. The trophy cannot be missed.
steps: Follow Kenton's mission strand on the map.
Complete Kenton's final mission.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade). Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide:
Complete Billy's final mission. Billy's strand is one of the character finales in the second stage of the roadmap — play his missions in order until the strand closes.

The trophy pops at the final mission's end screen. If Billy's marker is not on the map yet, keep playing the story; character strands open as the story advances. Nothing here can be missed.
steps: Follow Billy's mission strand on the map.
Complete Billy's final mission.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade). Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide:
Complete 8 stranger mission strands across Leonida. Strangers are the side characters marked on the map — each strand is a short chain of missions, and you need 8 whole strands finished, not 8 single missions.

Pick up every stranger marker you pass while playing the story, and finish each strand before moving on, so you do not lose track of which ones are done. The count is 8, and the official description gives no list of which strangers count — the in-game stranger markers are the list to work from.
steps: Find stranger markers across Leonida.
Complete 8 full stranger mission strands.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade); PSN count 8 strands — PSNProfiles. Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide:
Complete Randy's final mission. Randy's strand is another character finale — play his missions in order until the strand ends and the trophy pops at the final mission's end screen.

If Randy's missions are not available yet, they will open as the story advances. Nothing here can be missed.
steps: Follow Randy's mission strand on the map.
Complete Randy's final mission.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade). Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide:
Complete Tyrone's final mission. Tyrone's strand closes the set of named character finales in this guide's second stage — play his missions in order to the end.

The trophy pops at the final mission's end screen, with no extra condition. It cannot be missed.
steps: Follow Tyrone's mission strand on the map.
Complete Tyrone's final mission.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade). Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide:
Meditate at all 18 meditation spots across Leonida. Each spot is a place where the game offers the meditate action — visit it, meditate, and move on to the next.

The count is 18, and the spots are spread across the state, so this is a map-coverage trophy: work region by region and tick each spot off as you go. The official description does not list the spots, so the meditation markers in the game are the list — do not guess at locations the description does not name. Nothing here can be missed; spots stay available.
steps: Find meditation spots on the map.
Meditate at all 18 spots.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade); PSN count 18 spots — PSNProfiles. Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide:
Hunt a unique animal for Bret. Bret is a named character with a hunting strand — follow their missions until the hunt for the unique animal comes up, then take the animal down.

Unique means one of a kind: there is a specific animal to find, not just any animal in the wild. The official description names the character (Bret) but not the animal or where it lives, so follow Bret's strand and its in-game markers rather than guessing at a species or a spot. The trophy cannot be missed.
steps: Follow Bret's mission strand.
Hunt the unique animal the strand points to.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade). Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide:
Complete 3 full collectible card sets. Cards are scattered across Leonida — pick them up as you explore, and a set is complete when every card in it is found.

Three sets is the target, not every set in the game, so stop at three if the rest can wait. Work region by region and use the in-game card checklist to see which sets are closest to complete. The official description does not say how many cards are in a set or where they are, so the game's own card tracker is the list to trust. Nothing here can be missed.
steps: Collect cards as you explore Leonida.
Complete 3 full card sets, checking the in-game card tracker.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade); PSN count 3 sets — PSNProfiles. Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide:
Use the WAiNK feature at 100 locations. WAiNK is the in-game photo or tagging action — the count is cumulative, so every location you have already done counts toward the 100.

This is a pure volume trophy: fold it into normal exploration by WAiNK-ing at every new place you reach, and finish the remainder by sweeping the map region by region. The official description gives the target (100) but no list of locations, so the in-game WAiNK markers and counter are the guide. Nothing can be missed.
steps: WAiNK at locations as you explore.
Reach 100 WAiNK locations, checking the in-game counter.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade); PSN count 100 locations — PSNProfiles. Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide:
Complete 50 challenges. Challenges are the game's side objectives — the count is cumulative across every kind of challenge, so story missions, activities and exploration all feed it.

Do not grind this alone: by the time the story, the stranger strands and the activity trophies are done, a large part of the 50 will already be banked. Then open the game's challenge list and pick off the easiest remaining ones. The official description gives the target (50) and nothing else, so the in-game challenge list is the checklist.
steps: Play the story and activities; challenges accumulate.
Open the in-game challenge list and finish the easiest remaining ones to 50.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade); PSN count 50 — PSNProfiles. Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.missableWhy: It needs a 4-star wanted level while your partner is with you, then a clean escape — a moment that only happens when the story puts the two of you together. Do it during a partner mission, before the story moves on.
trophies.guide:
With your partner beside you, build a 4-star wanted level and then lose it and escape. The partner matters: the trophy needs the two of you together when the heat comes off.

The surest time is during a story mission where your partner is with you — cause enough trouble to reach 4 stars, then break line of sight, hide, and wait for the wanted level to clear while your partner is still with you. If the story moves past the partner missions, the chance may not come back, so do this while partner missions are still in front of you. That is why this guide flags it missable.
steps: During a mission with your partner beside you, reach a 4-star wanted level.
Break line of sight and escape until the wanted level clears, with your partner still with you.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade). Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.missableWhy: It needs your partner with you for three shop robberies in a row, keeping the same wanted level throughout. Partner missions are the reliable time to have them beside you — do it while those missions are still available.
trophies.guide:
With your partner, rob 3 shops one after another without losing your wanted level. Back-to-back means in one run, and the wanted level must survive all three robberies — if it clears, the run is broken and you start again.

Pick three shops close together, plan the route before the first robbery, and move fast between them with your partner. The reliable time to have your partner beside you is during partner missions, so do this while those missions are still in front of you — that is why it is flagged missable. A failed run can be retried, but only while a partner is available.
steps: With your partner beside you, pick three nearby shops.
Rob all three in one run without losing your wanted level.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade). Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide:
Discover 100 different vehicles. Discovering means encountering a vehicle type for the first time — the count grows as you meet new cars, bikes, boats and aircraft across Leonida, and it is cumulative.

Just play and explore: story missions, races and free-roam driving all feed the count. If it stalls near the end, visit the places where rare vehicles gather — the airport, the docks, car meets — and check the in-game vehicle list for what you have not seen yet. Nothing can be missed.
steps: Drive, race and explore; new vehicle types register as discovered.
Visit the airport, docks and car meets for the rarer types, to 100.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade); PSN count 100 vehicles — PSNProfiles. Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide:
Take down 5 enemies during one use of Combat Focus. Combat Focus is the game's slow-down aiming mode — activate it when a group of enemies is in front of you and drop five before it ends.

Wait for a firefight with at least five enemies clustered together, trigger Combat Focus, and work through them quickly. If you fall short, the attempt simply does not count — try again at the next firefight. The official description pins down no location, so any fight with enough enemies will do.
steps: Find a firefight with at least 5 enemies together.
Activate Combat Focus and take down 5 enemies before it ends.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade); PSN count 5 enemies — PSNProfiles. Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.missableWhy: It describes a single unscheduled departure from Vice City International Airport — a one-off moment tied to the airport, not a repeatable activity. Do it the first time you are at VCIA with a plane available.
trophies.guide:
Leave Vice City International Airport in a plane without a scheduled flight — an unscheduled departure. In plain terms: get a plane at VCIA and take off with it yourself, rather than boarding a flight the game scheduled.

Do this the first time you are at the airport with a plane you can take — the description reads like a single moment, not a repeatable activity, so do not assume it will still be available later. That is why this guide flags it missable. The official description names the airport (VCIA) and nothing else, so no runway or aircraft is claimed here.
steps: Go to VCIA.
Take a plane and make an unscheduled departure.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade). Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide:
Survive or succeed in a Rhino tank — the description is a joke, not an instruction, so read it as a tank moment: get into a Rhino and live through the chaos it brings.

Rhinos are the military tanks of the series, and the wanted level that follows stealing one is the point: grab one, survive the response, and the trophy should pop for the tank encounter itself. The official description gives no objective beyond the joke, so no specific feat is claimed here — the in-game objective text, when the moment arrives, is the real instruction. It is not flagged missable: tanks and the wanted response can be found again.
steps: Find a Rhino tank.
Get in and survive the response it draws.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade). Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide:
Rob a jewelry store and get away without being detected at any point. Undetected means no alarm, no spotted camera, no guard raising the alarm — a clean run from entry to exit.

Plan before you go in: watch the guards and cameras, move when they look away, take the goods and leave the same way. If you are spotted, the run is spoiled — leave, let the heat die down, and try the robbery again. It is not flagged missable, because jewelry store robberies can be attempted again.
steps: Pick a jewelry store and watch its guards and cameras.
Rob it and leave without being detected at any point.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade). Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide:
Rob 5 bank vaults and escape from each one. Each vault counts only when you get away after the robbery — being caught or killed after the vault means that vault does not count.

Bank vaults are the bigger, planned robberies: expect a vault to crack, a getaway, and a wanted level to lose. Do them one at a time, with a getaway vehicle and a route planned before you start, and the count builds to 5. The official description gives the target (5) but no bank locations, so the bank markers in the game are the list.
steps: Find a bank vault robbery.
Rob the vault and escape; repeat for 5 vaults.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade); PSN count 5 vaults — PSNProfiles. Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide:
Rob an armored truck and escape. Armored trucks drive set routes around the map — intercept one, stop it, take the cash, and lose the wanted level that follows.

Block the truck's path, deal with its guards, grab the money and get away before the response closes in. Trucks keep appearing, so a failed attempt can simply be retried on the next one. The official description names no route or location, so watch the roads for the trucks themselves.
steps: Find an armored truck on the road.
Stop it, take the cash, and escape.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade). Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide:
Explore all 52 areas of Leonida. The state is divided into 52 named areas, and the trophy pops when you have set foot in every one of them.

This is the map-coverage trophy: drive the roads, visit the towns, the beaches, the swamps and the city, and the in-game map will show which areas are still unvisited. Fold it into the collectibles stage — every trip for a card, a meditation spot or a WAiNK location is also progress here. Nothing can be missed.
steps: Explore Leonida region by region.
Visit all 52 areas, checking the map for unvisited ones.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade); PSN count 52 areas — PSNProfiles. Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide:
Rob one illegal operation belonging to each of the 9 gangs. Gangs run illegal operations around Leonida — hit one operation per gang, and the trophy pops when the ninth gang's operation is robbed.

Keep a note of which gangs you have hit: nine is the target, and the official description does not name the gangs, so the operations you find in the game are the list. Rob an operation, escape, and move on to a different gang's territory. Nothing can be missed.
steps: Find illegal operations in gang territory.
Rob one operation for each of the 9 gangs.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade); PSN count 9 gangs — PSNProfiles. Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide:
Have a cocktail at a spot with a view on Ocean Beach. Ocean Beach is the beachfront strip of Vice City — find a bar or vendor there with a view of the water, order a cocktail, and enjoy it.

This is a location moment, not a challenge: go to Ocean Beach, find somewhere serving cocktails with a view, and the trophy pops when the drink is enjoyed. The official description names the place (Ocean Beach) but no specific bar, so use the beachfront bars in the game rather than a named spot this guide does not have. It cannot be missed.
steps: Go to Ocean Beach.
Order and enjoy a cocktail at a spot with a view.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade). Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide:
Drive a car through a vehicle showroom's window and out the other side — the classic GTA showroom smash. Get a car inside or at the front of a showroom, build speed, and smash straight out through the glass.

Any vehicle showroom will do; the description's “classic style” is the joke, not an extra condition — the smash itself is the trophy. If the first attempt does not register, try another showroom or a faster run-up. It cannot be missed.
steps: Find a vehicle showroom.
Drive a car through it and smash your way out.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade). Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide:
Bowl at the Kolt & Associates bowling alley. The description names the alley, so go there specifically — not just any bowling lane — and follow through on a bowl.

Play a game at that alley; the trophy is about the visit and the bowl, not a score. This is also one of the activity types for Master of None, so it does double duty. It cannot be missed.
steps: Go to the Kolt & Associates bowling alley.
Bowl a game there.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade). Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide:
Reach a partnership moment with mass appeal. The description is deliberately vague — it reads like a story beat where the partnership becomes public or celebrated, rather than a task with steps to follow.

Play the story and it will come to you; there is no action to take beyond reaching the beat. Because the description gives no objective, this guide claims no method for it — if it does not pop by the end of the story, check the in-game objective text around partnership missions. It is not flagged missable: story beats can be replayed.
steps: Play the story through its partnership beats.
The trophy pops at the story moment the description points to.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade). Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.missableWhy: It tracks choices — PSN counts them toward 500 — and some choices only happen once, in one playthrough. Make choices as they come and do not skip decision moments; a skipped choice may not return.
trophies.guide:
Make choices in the game — the description says “choices made (for better or worse)”, and PSN tracks a count toward 500. Every decision the game offers counts, so take the choices as they come instead of avoiding them.

Choices appear in missions, conversations and side moments; the count builds over the whole playthrough. Because some choices only happen once, a decision skipped or rushed past may not come back — that is why this guide flags it missable. Play naturally, choose when asked, and the trophy follows the count.
steps: Take the choices the game offers as they come.
Keep choosing until the tracked count is reached.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade); PSN count 500 choices — PSNProfiles. Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.missableWhy: It needs a success on a second try — a retry moment that only counts when the first attempt fails and the second lands. If you succeed first time, that chance is gone; look for a retryable moment and let the first attempt fail cleanly.
trophies.guide:
Succeed on a second attempt — “second time's the charm”. The trophy is about a retry: fail once, then succeed on the very next try at the same thing.

The catch is that succeeding first time gives you no second try, so this one needs a deliberate miss followed by a success at a retryable moment — a race, a challenge, a minigame. Pick something retryable, fail the first attempt, then win the second. That one-shot nature is why it is flagged missable: once a first-try success is banked, that moment is gone.
steps: Pick a retryable activity.
Fail the first attempt, then succeed on the second try.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade). Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.missableWhy: It describes a strange, one-off event — something you witness once, not a task you can repeat. Keep your eyes open while exploring, especially at odd hours and odd places; a missed sighting may not repeat.
trophies.guide:
Witness something strange — the description is a baffled “what the hell just happened?”, which reads like a one-off odd event in the world, not a task with steps.

There is no way to force this one from the description alone: explore widely, visit odd places at odd hours, and pay attention to strange encounters. Because it is a single sighting, a missed event may not repeat — that is why it is flagged missable. No location is claimed here, because the official description names none.
steps: Explore Leonida widely, including odd places and odd hours.
The trophy pops when the strange event is witnessed.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade). Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide:
Knock someone down with a melee attack from a moving vehicle — a melee drive-by. Drive past a pedestrian, swing a melee weapon from the vehicle, and connect.

Find a slow road with pedestrians, keep the vehicle moving, and time the swing as you pass. If you miss, just try the next passer-by — the attempt is endlessly repeatable, so it is not flagged missable. The official description pins down no location, so any road with pedestrians will do.
steps: Get a melee weapon and a vehicle.
Drive past a pedestrian and land a melee hit from the moving vehicle.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade). Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide:
Earn $250,000 by laundering Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills are the dirty cash from robberies — take them to your contacts, who clean them for a cut, and the cleaned total counts toward the $250,000.

Rob banks, trucks and stores to build up Marked Bills, then launder them steadily through contacts rather than hoarding them. The count is cumulative across the playthrough, so the robbery trophies in this guide feed it directly. The official description gives the target ($250,000) but names no contact, so use the contacts the game itself offers.
steps: Collect Marked Bills from robberies.
Launder them through your contacts until $250,000 is earned.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade); PSN target $250,000 — PSNProfiles. Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide:
Spend $100,000 across all shops. Every purchase in any shop counts — clothes, weapons, food, car parts — and the total is cumulative across the whole playthrough.

Just play and buy what you need: by the late game, weapons, vehicles and upgrades will have eaten a large part of the $100,000 already. If you are short at the end, buy the most expensive items you still want. Nothing can be missed.
steps: Buy gear, clothes, weapons and upgrades as you play.
Keep spending across shops until the total reaches $100,000.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade); PSN target $100,000 — PSNProfiles. Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide:
Buy all 8 garage properties. Garages are the properties that store your vehicles — find them for sale across Leonida and purchase each one.

Garages cost money, so save this for the late game when the robbery and laundering trophies have filled your wallet. The count is 8, and the official description does not list them, so the property markers in the game are the list. Nothing can be missed.
steps: Find garage properties for sale across Leonida.
Purchase all 8.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade); PSN count 8 garages — PSNProfiles. Guidance from the official description.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide:
Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. The app is the in-game vehicle service — open it, pick a vehicle you own or have found, and register it; repeat for 10 different vehicles.

Any 10 vehicles will do, so register the ones you already drive rather than hunting for rare ones. The official description gives the target (10) and names the app (Scooter Bros), and nothing else — the app itself shows how to register. It cannot be missed.
steps: Open the Scooter Bros app.
Register 10 vehicles through it.
trophies.sources: Official list — Exophase and PSNProfiles (name, description, grade); PSN count 10 vehicles — PSNProfiles. Guidance from the official description.
